q-163048.name: Question 1
q-163048.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=x{y}^{2}-y,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-163048.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-y)={y}^{2}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-y)=2xy-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & 2xy-1\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2} & 2(0)(1)-1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-163048.html:
Question 1
?

For the transformation f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=xy2−y,x=[xy],

calculate f′ at a=[01].

a
[21]
b
[11]
c
[1−1]
d
[−11]
e
[10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(xy2−y)=y2,∂f∂y=∂∂y(xy2−y)=2xy−1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[y22xy−1]

and f′ at a=[0−1] is

f′(a)=[(1)22(0)(1)−1]=[1−1].

q-163034.name: Question 2
q-163034.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={e}^{xy},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
q-163034.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy})=y{e}^{xy}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})=x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].
$$

For the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=exy,x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[exey]
b
[eyex]

[yexyxexy]

[yeyxex]

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(exy)=yexy,∂f∂y=∂∂y(exy)=xexy

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[yexyxexy].

q-163100.name: Question 3
q-163100.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{xyz} \\ x+yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
q-163100.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xyz})=yz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xyz})=xz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xyz})=xy{e}^{xyz} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+yz)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+yz)=z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+yz)=y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}yz{e}^{xyz} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 & z & y\end{aligned}].
$$

q-163100.html:
Question 3
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[exyzx+yz],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[AAxzexyzxyexyz1AAAA]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
yzeyz, 0, and y
b
yzexyz, z, and y
c
xexyz, z, and z
d
exyz, 2x, and y
e
zexyz, z, and z
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f1∂z∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f2∂z]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(exyz)=yzexyz,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(exyz)=xzexyz,∂f1∂z=∂∂z(exyz)=xyexyz∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x+yz)=1,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x+yz)=z,∂f2∂z=∂∂z(x+yz)=y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[yzexyzxzexyzxyexyz1zy].

q-162942.name: Question 4
q-162942.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz) \\ {x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & \frac{1}{z} \\ \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & {x}^{2}z & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
q-162942.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)=2xyz,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \frac{1}{y} & \frac{1}{z} \\ 2xyz & {x}^{2}z & {x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[ln⁡(xyz)x2yz],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[1xAA1zAAx2zAA]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
x2y, 1x, and x2y
b
2xyz, 1y, and yz
c
2xyz, 1z, and y2z
d
x2y, 1z, and x2y
e
2xyz, 1y, and x2y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f1∂z∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f2∂z]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(ln⁡(xyz))=1x,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(ln⁡(xyz))=1y,∂f1∂z=∂∂z(ln⁡(xyz))=1z∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x2yz)=2xyz,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x2yz)=x2z,∂f2∂z=∂∂z(x2yz)=x2y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1x1y1z2xyzx2zx2y].

q-163074.name: Question 5
q-163074.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{xy+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
q-163074.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}} & -\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\frac{1}{2},\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\frac{1}{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{1}{4})+(-\frac{1}{4})=0.
$$

$$

$$

f(a)=[1−1],f′(a)=[0−1−11].

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

q-163083.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=2{x}_{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2{x}_{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+\pi +(-1)=\pi -1.
$$
